newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rains soak German fields, winter crops safe.
newsitem.headline: Rains soak German fields, winter crops safe.

text.p: Rainfall continues to disrupt German maize and sugar beet harvests but winter crops in the ground are not affected, the DWD meteorological office said in a weekly report on Thursday.
"Farmers can't get to the maize and beet on wet fields and this may cause some production losses," a DWD source said.
"But winter crops are developing well as temperatures are dropping, which retards growth ahead of complete dormancy."
DWD forecast maximum day temperatures around six degrees C in the period up to November 27, having recorded one to seven degrees and the first night frosts in the previous seven days.
The sugar beet compaign continued speedily, and is more than two-thirds completed.
Harvested beet is stored alongside the fields and is being gradually driven to factories.
The sugar industry association WVZ on Tuesday said final deliveries might be down at 25.80 million tonnes compared with 26.05 million in 1995/96 because of the cold and rain.
Wet new crop maize was only reaching markets after delays and with drying costs added, traders said.
This could threaten its competitiveness versus feed wheat.
Germany expects a 2.84 million tonnes maize crop after 2.40 million in 1995.
Snow in neighbouring France has slowed a bumper maize harvest, part of which is expected to find its way into Germany and compete with domestic supplies.
